transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded 2026-06-17 14:30 UTC, Duration 68 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Julian Park (Redwood CSM), Liam O'Connor (Kiwi Aviation - Head of Data), Amira Patel (Platform Eng), Carlos Mendes (Security Lead), Sofia Ramires (CTO)

Summary: See summary field above.

Topics: onboarding timeline, private vs hosted, VPC peering, SOC2/KMS, pilot metrics

Questions: (at end) quick Q/A and next steps recap

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll kick off — this is the handoff from sales to CS/SE — I'm Maya, AE on the deal. Quick roll call?
[00:12] Liam: Liam here, hi — Head of Data at Kiwi Aviation.
[00:16] Amira: Amira, platform eng.
[00:19] Carlos: Carlos, security.
[00:21] Sofia: Sofia, CTO.
[00:23] Priya: Priya Singh, solutions engineer from Redwood.
[00:25] Julian: Julian Park, CSM, i'll be running the onboarding sprints.

[00:35] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda — 1) timeline and sprint cadence, 2) network options (hosted api vs dedicated/private VPC), 3) security artifacts (SAML, KMS, audit logs), 4) pilot success criteria and next steps. Anything to add? 
[00:47] Sofia: No, looks good.

[01:05] Priya: I'll jump in on the technical part, primarily to validate assumptions from the POC and go through what a private deployment would look like. Quick note, some of the notes from demo call said you had really high peak qps during booking spikes? I think sales put 1k qps number — is that right?
[01:26] Liam: Yeah, that's approximate. During promotions we see, um, bursts to around 900–1,100 qps for short windows. Average is more like 60 to 120.
[01:36] Priya: Okay, good. That matters for batching and autoscale config. Also sequence lengths — are you mostly short prompts or sending larger context from booking histories?
[01:47] Amira: It's mixed — nav queries are short but we pass passenger context for personalization sometimes, can be 400–800 tokens on the long tail.

[02:05] Priya: Got it. So two workload modes — short low-latency and occasional long-seq personalization. We typically recommend routing those to different model bundles or using prefix caching to reduce cost. On private deployments, we can do dedicated pools to keep latency predictable.

[03:00] Carlos: On security side, big concern is PII in prompts. We need assurance around encryption at rest, KMS integrations, and also audit logs retention for compliance. Do you have HSM/KMS options?
[03:17] Priya: Yes, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we also integrate with common cloud KMS and have an HSM option for enterprise add-on. We'll share the security pack with details.

[04:02] Carlos: What about SSO? We need SAML SSO and role-based access controls — we can't have broad admin rights.
[04:12] Julian: Absolutely. We support SAML and OIDC, and RBAC is configurable at route and model level. We'll capture the exact roles you want in the runbook.

[04:45] Maya: For the network choices — to reiterate, two paths: 1) Hosted API — fastest to get going, less ops work; 2) Private / VPC — more control for data residency and no egress of prompts through public endpoints. For Kiwi, I think data residency and PII routing push you toward private, is that fair?
[05:09] Sofia: Yes, we're leaning private, especially for production. Pilot could start on hosted but long-term needs VPC.

[05:30] Priya: If we do private, two options: VPC peering or private link — depends on your cloud provider. We have customers on AWS using VPC peering with a NAT-less path. A note — sometimes transcripts from infra calls show VPC as V-B-C in auto-transcripts, haha.

[06:00] (laughter)

[06:12] Priya: We'll also want to validate routing for third-party tools — analytics and logging — so you don't accidentally send PII outside. We'll provide a network diagram template and ask for a contact from your infra team.
[06:29] Amira: That's me, Amira will take that.

[07:00] Priya: Cool. For latency SLO — what's acceptable? In the sales thread Maya mentioned sub-300ms 95th; is that still the right bar?
[07:12] Liam: We'd like 95th < 250ms for short prompts. For long personalization calls we can tolerate more, say 600–800ms.
[07:24] Priya: Okay, we'll treat those as separate routes — short prompt model pinned to low-latency configuration, long-seq to a quantized variant with higher throughput. Note: quantization may trade small quality delta for throughput; we'll include that in the evals.

[08:05] Carlos: We need to understand data retention and the ability to disable retention at rest. Can we do no-log mode for certain routes?
[08:15] Priya: Yes, Redwood offers per-route log retention controls. For Private there's also a config to disable persistence for KV cache and request logs. We'll show the exact toggles in the security doc.

[09:00] Maya: On the pilot scope — propose: 1) 2-week sandbox to validate network & auth, 2) 4-week pilot on private deployment with a production-ish traffic replay, 3) final tuning and SLA agreement. Does that timeline align with your capacity?
[09:22] Sofia: Timeline overall looks fine. We have a governance board meeting on 7/7, would like results before then ideally.
[09:31] Julian: That pushes us to start sandbox by the week of 6/22 so we can have pilot feedback by early July.

[10:00] Priya: To make the sandbox quick, we'll need sample traffic (anonymized), a list of routes you want to test, and a contact for networking. Also note — for on-prem or airgapped customers we have an on-prem package which has additional ops steps.
[10:21] Amira: We'll provide anonymized traffic — can scrub PII. I can coordinate with Carlos for compliance.

[11:05] Carlos: On compliance, do you have ISO or SOC reports we can provide to auditors?
[11:12] Maya: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II attestations and ISO 27001 docs; will send links. Also we have an SOC summary and a customer-facing security pack with network diagrams and KMS/HSM options.
[11:28] Priya: And we have a privacy whitepaper that covers PII handling and redaction suggestions.

[12:00] Liam: One deeper question — we do some reranking and embeddings for search personalization. Can Redwood host embeddings and also provide a rerank route? We want to keep embeddings in our account.
[12:14] Priya: Embeddings are supported; we can host them in the private deployment or give you an option to run embeddings in your VPC while using Redwood for generation. For reranking, we support a rerank API pattern — if you want full control, you can run the embedding store locally and call Redwood for scoring.

[13:00] Amira: Cost discussion — is dedicated capacity billed monthly? Or per-token for hosted?
[13:08] Maya: Hosted is usage per-token; Dedicated/reserved capacity is monthly commit. We can provide a blended estimate for pilot traffic. For steady-state, dedicated is often more predictable for unit economics.

[14:22] (background noise, brief crosstalk)

[14:45] Priya: I want to call out one thing from the POC — we hit an edge case on KV cache invalidation when session tokens change quickly. We'll note a recommended cache TTL of 30 seconds for your session-heavy flows.
[15:05] Liam: That might be ok, we'll have to test.

[16:00] (discussion about who owns runbook)
[16:12] Julian: We'll produce an onboarding runbook with owners. I'll be the runbook owner, but we'll have Priya as technical owner for infra notes.
[16:24] Priya: I'll draft the network diagram and sample NACLs. Also will include guidance for model pinning and quantization choices.

[18:00] Carlos: Regarding encryption, we need to see key rotation policies and whether logs can be pushed to our SIEM. Do you support pushing audit logs to customer-managed S3 or a logging endpoint?
[18:18] Priya: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to customer-managed storage and integrated with common SIEMs. We'll document the schema and retention controls in the pack.

[20:00] Sofia: Any blockers from Redwood side we should be aware of?
[20:08] Maya: No major blockers — main things are confirming network path, traffic sample, and security paperwork — which we'll turn around quickly.

[22:00] (Priya shares screen / reference to doc link)
[22:12] Priya: I'm dropping the security pack link in the chat now — https://redwood.example.com/security/pack-kiwi (note: placeholder). Also the onboarding runbook template: https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/onboarding-template

[24:00] Amira: Great, i'll assign someone to the network diagram.

[26:00] (discussion of success metrics and acceptance criteria)
[26:20] Liam: Success metrics: 95th latency under 250ms for short routes, error rate < 0.5%, and ability to redact PII automatically before logs are persisted.
[26:34] Priya: We'll add those to the pilot acceptance matrix and run the traffic replay to validate.

[30:00] (filler chatter about internal calendars)

[31:00] Julian: I'll send calendar invites for weekly 30 minute onboarding cadence, first one on 2026-06-23. We'll also have a technical deep-dive post-sandbox with SEs.

[33:00] Carlos: On legal side, we may need a data processing addendum and some specific contractual language around no-persistence for certain endpoints.
[33:18] Maya: Understood, legal team will send DPA template; i'll include the legal contact.

[35:00] Priya: Operational note — if you want to A/B test models during pilot, we support canary and traffic split routing. We can also fall back to a smaller model if capacity spikes.
[35:18] Amira: That fallback behavior is important — we don't want bookings to fail if model is slow.

[37:00] Sofia: Is there an in-console view for trace/span level latency per model? We want to see token-level cost breakdowns.
[37:12] Julian: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route token breakdowns, model-level latency histograms and traces. We'll include screenshots in the onboarding deck.

[40:00] (brief pause)

[40:30] Priya: Ok, practical next steps — I'll schedule a private-deploy feasibility call with Carlos and Amira early next week. Maya will share the security pack today. Julian will set up the weekly cadence. Amira will send initial traffic sample.

[41:12] Liam: One more thing — regional residency: we need EU-only storage for EU traffic. Is that supported?
[41:21] Priya: Yes, we can pin deployments to EU regions; private deployments can be hosted in region-specific clusters.

[42:00] Carlos: Also curious about disaster recovery — RPO/RTO for dedicated pools?
[42:10] Priya: We'll include typical RPO/RTO numbers in the SLA doc; for dedicated reserved capacity we can negotiate stricter RTOs.

[44:00] Sofia: Ok, i'm satisfied — sounds like we have an action plan. Quick recap please?

[44:12] Maya: Recap: 1) Send security pack + SOC2 (Maya) by 6/20; 2) Priya to prototype network diagram & private-deploy feasibility and schedule meeting 6/22 week; 3) Kiwi to deliver anonymized traffic and route list by 6/24; 4) Julian to set weekly onboarding cadence starting 6/23; 5) Legal to exchange DPA drafts. Any additions?
[44:55] Carlos: No, that's good.
[45:00] Amira: Good.

[46:00] (wrap up, thanks and sign-off)
[46:12] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with links and the action items. Talk soon.
[46:20] Liam: Thanks.

(End of recording)
